newsitem.title: UK: Norwich Union details share offer.
newsitem.headline: Norwich Union details share offer.

text.p: British insurer Norwich Union on Thursday announced details of its planned flotation in June, saying that the 2.9 million qualifying members of the society would receive a total of 1.3 billion free shares.

Norwich Union said in a statement that it estimated the shares would have traded at between 220 and 265 pence each as at February 28. Norwich Union intends to raise around 1.75 billion pounds ($2.8 billion) of new capital through an offer of additional shares, 1.5 billion pounds of which will be paid into its with-profit life insurance fund.
life policies will receive a minimum of 300 free shares, and non-profit members will received a fixed allocation of 150 shares.

Norwich Union, which reported pre-tax profit in 1996 of 483 million pounds, said it believed the improvement in the life and pensions market would be to the long-term benefit to the group, but said results of its general insurance arm would continue to be affected by pricing pressure in 1997, particularly in Britain.
"We firmly believe that flotation is the best way forward for Norwich Union and its members," chief executive Allan Bridgewater said in a statement.

"The financial information published today demonstrates the strength of our business and we see many opportunities for the future development of Norwich Union. Following flotation, we will be in an even stronger position to take advantage of these opportunities," he said.

Norwich Union, which had pro forma net assets of 4.48 billion pounds as at December 31, 1996, said the floation would be voted on at a members' meeting on April 18 after which it needs court approval at a hearing set for April 23. The group expects the prospectus for the additional share offer to be issued in May and flotation to take place in June. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
